page.title: Microsoft Teamss
page.subtitle: Route workflow, alert, and backup events to a Microsoft Teams channel via an Adaptive Card posted to an Incoming Webhook connector URL. The plugin handles Test (posts a real Adaptive Card with the configured themeColor) and Send (posts Title + Message as the Adaptive Card body) — there is no OAuth flow because Incoming Webhook connectors are URL-only credentials.
page.registerHint: Add a channel from the host's Notifications > Channels page and pick "teams" as the channel_type.

help.webhookUrl: Incoming Webhook connector URL from Microsoft Teams. Channel menu (...) → Connectors → Incoming Webhook → Configure → copy the URL. The UUID in the URL is the auth credential — treat it as a secret.
help.themeColor: Hex color (no #) used for the Adaptive Card's left accent stripe. Defaults to Teams brand purple (5059C9).

error.noWebhook: Webhook URL is required. Paste the Incoming Webhook connector URL from Teams.

form.webhookBody: The plugin posts an **Adaptive Card** to the configured webhook URL. The notification Title becomes a bold TextBlock header (Medium size), the Message becomes a wrapping TextBlock body, and the card carries an optional themeColor on its left accent stripe. Teams renders the card inline in the channel — no install, no app permissions, no consent flow.
form.themeIntro: Teams renders the configured `themeColor` as a colored stripe along the left edge of every Adaptive Card. Use it to color-code by environment or severity:
form.themeRed: `DC3545` — red, for production alerts / pager notifications.
form.themeOutro: Use the 6-character hex form without the leading `#` — Adaptive Cards ignore the `#` and treat it as part of the color name.
form.securityHelp: The UUID in the URL IS the credential
form.securityIntro: Anyone holding the webhook URL can post to the channel — there is no separate token, no signing key. Treat the URL as a secret:
form.securityGit: Don't commit it to git (even in private repos).
form.securityShare: Don't paste it into Slack, email, or ticket comments where the recipient doesn't need to post to your channel.
form.securityRotate: Rotate by deleting the connector in Teams, creating a new one, and pasting the new URL here. Old URLs fail with a Teams-side 410 Gone the moment the connector is removed.
form.testBody: The Test call posts a real Adaptive Card (`Title: McHarbor test notification`, body `This is a test message from McHarbor.`) to your channel. Teams returns `200 OK` on a working webhook; the plugin translates any non-2xx into a structured error showing the upstream status + first 256 bytes of the response body. The card lands in the channel as a visible message — let subscribers know before clicking Test so it doesn't generate a false-positive alert ticket.

step1.body: Open Microsoft Teams and navigate to the channel you want alerts to land in. Incoming Webhook connectors are scoped to a single channel — repeat the steps below for each channel you want to receive alerts in.

step2.body: Click the channel menu (••• next to the channel name) → Connectors. Scroll down to Incoming Webhook in the list and click Configure. Give the connector a name (e.g. McHarbor Alerts) and optionally upload an image that will appear next to every card the connector posts.

step3.body: Click Create. Teams displays the webhook URL — copy it now. The URL contains the connector UUID which is the auth credential; you will not see it again after closing the dialog. Paste it into the Webhook URL field on the left.

step4.body: Click Done to close the configuration dialog. The connector is now active and the channel will start accepting POSTs to the URL. There is no separate "publish" step — Teams activates connectors immediately.

step5.body: Optional: set Theme Color to a 6-character hex (no #) to colour the Adaptive Card's left accent stripe. Defaults to Teams brand purple (5059C9). Useful for visual scanning across multiple environments or alert severities.

step6.body: Save the channel. Click Test connection — the plugin posts an Adaptive Card with Title "McHarbor test notification" and body "This is a test message from McHarbor." to your channel. The card should appear within 1-2 seconds.

step7.body: If Test returns 400, the payload is malformed — double-check you did not modify the Webhook URL (append query parameters, etc.). If 404, the connector was deleted in Teams after you copied the URL — re-create it and update the field. If you see a 200 OK in the response but no card in Teams, the connector is configured for a different channel than the one you're looking at.

step8.body: To restrict which channels can post: open the connector's configuration dialog in Teams and use the Restrict to channels option. This is per-connector and is a Teams-side setting; the plugin cannot enforce it.

step9.body: Once the channel is saved, route workflow or alert events to it from Settings > Notifications > Rules. Teams delivery is fire-and-forget: a failed POST is logged in the audit log and surfaced in the host toast, but the host does not retry.
